  "headline": "Intake established the service outcome, test requirement, and defaults for unattended delivery.",

  "answers": [
    {"id": "K1.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "Organisers create events and people reserve seats through an HTTP service."},
    {"id": "K1.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "HTTP requests create an event with a seat capacity, accept reservations within that capacity, and reject reservations that would exceed it."},
    {"id": "K2.1", "basis": "S1", "answer": "Build the small Python HTTP service and include tests; deployment, a user interface, and features beyond event creation and reservations are outside the request."},
    {"id": "K2.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "The request says the repository is empty, so no existing application behaviour is identified to preserve; discovery should confirm the checkout."},
    {"id": "K3.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume JSON requests and responses: POST /events accepts {\"seats\": integer} and returns an event ID and capacity; POST /events/{event_id}/reservations accepts {\"seats\": integer} and returns a reservation ID and reserved quantity. Discovery checks the runtime before these names and shapes are finalized."},
    {"id": "K3.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume 201 for creation, 400 for malformed or invalid input, 404 for an unknown event, and 409 for insufficient remaining seats; errors use a JSON message."},
    {"id": "K4.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "An event has a positive whole-number capacity; each reservation requests a positive whole number of seats; successful reservations cannot exceed capacity, including under concurrent requests."},
    {"id": "K4.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Missing, malformed, non-integer, boolean, zero, or negative seat counts are invalid; an unknown event ID cannot be reserved."},
    {"id": "K5.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume the service owns event and reservation state in process memory for the lifetime of the process; state ends on restart."},
    {"id": "K5.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume no authentication or private-data requirement: callers receive their request's result, and no listing or retrieval endpoint is required. Serialize capacity changes so concurrent reservations cannot oversell; restart clears state."},
    {"id": "K6.1", "basis": "inspect", "answer": "Discovery must identify the available Python 3 version; assume the service targets that version."},
    {"id": "K6.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume Python standard-library dependencies are sufficient; no other dependency is required by the request."},
    {"id": "K6.3", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume a local HTTP listener with a documented configurable port; discovery determines the available execution environment."},
    {"id": "K7.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Keep reservation and capacity rules separable from HTTP handling so they can be tested independently."},
    {"id": "K8.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume Python's unittest framework and python -m unittest discover as the test command."},
    {"id": "K8.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "Tests send HTTP requests to a running service and observe event creation, successful reservation, invalid input, unknown events, and capacity rejection, including concurrent contention."},
    {"id": "K9.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Deliver runnable source and tests in the run's checkout; local execution requires Python and permission to bind a local port. No deployed target is named."},
    {"id": "K10.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Assume ordinary local use with no specified throughput, accessibility, interface-polish, or security targets; do not add a user interface or authentication."},
    {"id": "K11.1", "basis": "default", "answer": "Overselling, ambiguous API expectations, or loss of in-memory state may cause failure or rejection."},
    {"id": "K11.2", "basis": "default", "answer": "An early HTTP test covering capacity and concurrent reservations, plus review of the recorded API and storage defaults, would expose these risks."}

  "summary": "S1 — Fact: deliver a small Python HTTP event-and-seat reservation service in the run checkout for organisers and people using its HTTP entry points; assumption: one process holds volatile state, callers have no authenticated identity, reservation requests specify a seat quantity, and capacity changes are serialized; these defaults rule out durable storage, identity-based access and shared state across independent processes; discovery owns confirming the checkout, installed Python, local binding access and runtime-provided capabilities before implementation, which blocks final runtime and launch choices; discovery owns checking any available project documentation for API, identity, privacy, sharing and lifetime requirements before replacing the recorded defaults, which blocks only choices that conflict with evidence; no team, workspace, channel, internal site, private repository, owner, ambiguous term or sensitive locator is named as a source hint; no prior run or deployed target is identified; the isolated source checkout remains at its snapshot until final return, when the delivered source becomes visible, and a deployed outcome would exist only after release.
